content:
Completed a Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Lawvere's fixed-point theorem at the CCC level — not in Set/Type, but in an arbitrary cartesian closed category using Cartesian Monoidal Category and MonoidalClosed. 985 lines across 8 files, zero sorry, clean lake build.

The formalization includes:

  • lawvere_fixed_point in an arbitrary CCC (80 lines, full calc chain through monoidal coherence) 
  • Verified instantiation at C = Type u via SetInstantiation.lean, with rfl consistency proof against the direct diagonal argument                        
  • Application to quantum contextuality: PR box in the Bell (2,2,2) scenario proved contextual via a Liar cycle bridge to the Lawvere diagonal          
  • A three-way taxonomy classifying Lawvere instances as pure cardinality Cantor), structural diagonal (Bell), or self-referential (Gödel)
    Paper: https://osf.io/bgrf8/files/79qyu

I've seen comments here suggesting that people really, really, really shouldn't ask for arXiv endorsements on Zulip (see eg #maths > Knuth's Torus Decompositions (m=4, 6) @ 💬 - it's apparently against arXiv's policy to publicly farm for endorsement). On a selfish note, the proof for CCC is far from the most general https://doi.org/10.32408/compositionality-5-8

I can't find it again, but someone already formalised the result in my paper, but perhaps not published it, since it's so short. Moreover, Martin Escardó also has https://martinescardo.github.io/TypeTopology/Various.LawvereFPT.html so......
Aha, here it is: https://mathstodon.xyz/@highergeometer/112098277610968736 (14 lines, no axioms, March 2024)
By the way, Barreto's paper has been very much excoriated on the category theory zulip as AI-generated slop that shouldn't have made it past the submission phase on the arXiv, please don't trust it.
For the benefit of others, @mdnestor 's formalisation of Lawvere's FPT and variants (including due to Yanofsky, and myself) is available here: https://github.com/mdnestor/LawvereFixedPoint
